findings.text: the module fixture builds the figure in memory from the committed receipt and no test calls renderer.render_only or reads the published file, so the deliverable the plan cites, docs/figures/multi-unit-limiter-wall/wall-units.png, is tied to the renderer by no assertion; a regression in save() or a stale committed PNG would leave all four tests green.

the no-gridline half of the axis-off check reads get_xgridlines() visibility, which matplotlib leaves False by default (measured: a bare plt.subplots axes reports 6 xgridlines, all visible False), so that assertion passes on an axes that never called set_axis_off; the load-bearing assertion for the rule is the axison check at line 50, and the gridline check only fires against the specific regression of calling grid(True) again.

build_receipt reads jt-60sa_md at DD 4.1.0 and writes the receipt the gate then renders from, but the node records no log of that IDS read, so the receipt's five-unit closure vector is not independently attested by the node's own evidence; it is corroborated only because tests/test_wall_units.py:83-84 already pins the same description to vertex counts 89 6 6 10 8 and closures true false false false false against the same jt-60sa_md description at the same DD 4.1.0.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 8dcc0b7a; f072043fd adds the renderer, the test and the regenerated PNG, 633eb3e96 adds the receipt and the SVG, 734ec8f48 adds the plan and evidence landing paragraphs; no production module under nova/ is modified.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names a render from the committed receipt, PNG and SVG written, and a test asserting both panels axis-off with no gridlines, five distinct right-panel units with closure flags matching the description, and the left panel's two units; tests/test_wall_units_render.py:46-91 asserts each of those and the manifest records the run and its 4-passed result.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that wall-units.png is regenerated by a committed renderer with the axis off and the five JT-60SA units distinguishable; benchmarks/wall_units_render.py draws both panels through poloidal_axes and draw_panel, and the committed docs/figures/multi-unit-limiter-wall/wall-units.svg carries all five unit colours (3366cc, cc0000, cc7722, 2e7d32, 7b1fa2) and nine dashes, so the published figure does show five distinct units with the axis off.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory; it states status complete, commits f072043fd, 633eb3e96 and 734ec8f48, the gate command with its 4-passed result, the negative control's 1-failed-3-passed result, and the receipt's closure vector counts 89 6 6 10 8, each of which I reproduced from the named artefacts.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read from the dispatch fence and repeated in the manifest; the three commits touch only benchmarks/wall_units_render.py, tests/test_wall_units_render.py, the files under docs/figures/multi-unit-limiter-wall/, docs/plans/multi-unit-limiter-wall.html and docs/evidence/archive/multi-unit-limiter-wall-landed.html, every one inside the manifest's orientation_write_paths.

justifications.durability: the distinctness assertion at tests/test_wall_units_render.py:73 would redden if draw_panel stopped assigning per-unit colours, which the declared negative control demonstrates at 1 failed and 3 passed, but nothing in tests/test_wall_units_render.py renders to disk or reads the published figure, so a stale or hand-edited docs/figures/multi-unit-limiter-wall/wall-units.png passes the gate unchanged.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_wall_units_render.py:46-91 asserts the axis-off, the five distinct styles and the receipt's closure flags, its 4-passed log is on disk at the run directory and I reproduced it in the reviewed worktree; the deduction is that the no-gridline assertion at tests/test_wall_units_render.py:54 does not discriminate, since matplotlib's default gridlines are already invisible, and the receipt's fidelity to jt-60sa_md has no build log of its own.
justifications.fit: benchmarks/wall_units_render.py and tests/test_wall_units_render.py are named for the two-unit fixture and the renderer rather than for any plan item, both commits carry a conventional subject and a body, and the receipt-fed renderer follows the idiom of benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py and benchmarks/exact_clip_memory_scaling.py with no version, plan or author label in any symbol or path.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable at docs/figures/multi-unit-limiter-wall/wall-units.png is regenerated by the committed benchmarks/wall_units_render.py render_only through the shared painters, and my re-run at the reviewed tip drew both panels axis-off with the five units in five colours.
justifications.scope_discipline: git status --porcelain on the reviewed worktree at 734ec8f48 is empty, so the negative-control mutation named in the manifest was reverted, and every path in the three commits sits inside the manifest's declared write paths, with the plan and evidence landed on their own section.
